es: Escribir un párrafo que llegue a una conclusión prudente a partir de tres pistas, y descarte una alternativa con una prueba.

teaching.en: There is a ladder outside the café, and I can smell paint.
teaching.es: Hay una escalera fuera de la cafetería y huelo a pintura.
teaching.explanationEs: Primera pieza: pistas descritas como datos observables, sin interpretarlas.
segments: There is a ladder outside the
café, and I can smell paint.
teaching.audioText: There is a ladder outside the café, and I can smell paint.

teaching.en: These clues suggest that the café is closed for a renovation.
teaching.es: Estas pistas sugieren que la cafetería está cerrada por reformas.
teaching.explanationEs: Conclusión prudente con suggest: no «it is», sino lo que las pistas apuntan.
segments: These clues suggest that the café
teaching.audioText: These clues suggest that the café is closed for a renovation.

teaching.en: Apparently, the owner has ordered a new sign.
teaching.es: Al parecer, el dueño ha encargado un letrero nuevo.
teaching.explanationEs: Apparently marca información vista u oída que aún no se ha comprobado.
teaching.audioText: Apparently, the owner has ordered a new sign.

teaching.en: We can rule out the alternative that it is closing for good, because of the new sign.
teaching.es: Podemos descartar la alternativa de que cierre para siempre, por el letrero nuevo.
teaching.explanationEs: Rule out = descartar; explica la prueba con because of.
segments: We can rule out the alternative that it is
closing for good, because of the new sign.
teaching.audioText: We can rule out the alternative that it is closing for good, because of the new sign.

teaching.en: Each clue on its own is weak, but together they make a strong case.
teaching.es: Cada pista por sí sola es débil, pero juntas forman un caso sólido.
teaching.explanationEs: Varias pistas que coinciden pesan más que una sola.

but together they make a strong case.
teaching.audioText: Each clue on its own is weak, but together they make a strong case.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe una pista sin interpretarla.

choices.text: The shop has definitely closed for good.
There are boxes at the door and the light is off.

feedback.es: Una pista es un dato observable; las otras frases ya interpretan más de lo que se ve.

hint.es: Una pista describe lo que ves.

origin.text: Ves que la luz de la tienda está apagada y hay cajas en la puerta.

prompt.es: Completa: «Estas pistas sugieren que hay obras.»

feedback.es: Clues es plural y por eso va con these y suggest sin -s.

origin.text: These ___ suggest that there is a renovation.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Podemos descartar la lluvia porque la calle está seca.»

answer.text: We can rule out rain because the street is dry

feedback.es: Rule out + alternativa + because + prueba: descarta con un dato.

hint.es: Rule out lleva la alternativa detrás.

prompt.es: Elige la conclusión más prudente a partir de las pistas.

choices.text: These clues prove that the shop has closed for good.
These clues are a mystery with no answer.
These clues suggest that the shop is being painted.

feedback.es: Con pocas pistas, suggest presenta una conclusión posible; prove afirma demasiado.

origin.text: Pistas: hay una escalera, huele a pintura y el local lleva tres días cerrado.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cada pista por sí sola es débil» y «juntas forman un caso sólido».

feedback.es: Clue es la pista individual y case, el conjunto de pruebas que se suman.

sentences: Each ___ on its own is weak.

prompt.es: Escucha las pistas y elige la conclusión del hablante.

choices.text: He thinks that a shop will open soon.
He thinks that the shop is closing.
He thinks that the van is stolen.

feedback.es: Luces, furgoneta de reparto y ventanas tapadas son pistas de una tienda que prepara su apertura.

origin.audio: The lights are on at midnight, there is a delivery van outside, and the windows are covered with paper. I think the new shop is getting ready to open.

prompt.es: Escribe un párrafo con tres pistas, una conclusión y una alternativa descartada.

answer.text: The bakery has been closed for five days, and there are three clues. First, there is a delivery van at the door. Second, the front has new paint. Third, someone saw the owner with a new sign yesterday. These clues suggest that the bakery is not closing for good: it is probably having a renovation or moving to a bigger place. Of course, each clue on its own is weak, but together they make a strong case. We can rule out the alternative that the owner has left, because of the new sign. I will ask him tomorrow to be sure.
accepted: The bakery has been closed for five days, and there are three clues. First, there is a delivery van at the door. Second, the front has new paint. Third, someone saw the owner with a new sign yesterday. These clues suggest that the bakery is not closing for good: it is probably having a renovation or moving to a bigger place. Of course, each clue on its own is weak, but together they make a strong case. We can rule out the alternative that the owner has left, because of the new sign. I will ask him tomorrow to be sure.

The bakery has been shut for five days. I can see a van outside, fresh paint on the wall and a new sign in the owner's hand. Together, these clues point to a renovation, although I may be wrong. The bakery is unlikely to be closing for good, because nobody buys a new sign and paints a wall before leaving. I can rule out that alternative, and I will check with the owner tomorrow.

feedback.es: El párrafo debe describir las tres pistas, concluir con prudencia y descartar la alternativa del cierre definitivo.

origin.text: La panadería de tu barrio lleva cinco días cerrada. Pistas: hay una furgoneta de reparto en la puerta, han pintado la fachada y ayer vieron al dueño con un letrero nuevo. Escribe en inglés un párrafo de 80 a 140 palabras: describe las tres pistas, da una conclusión prudente (suggest, probably…) y descarta una alternativa, por ejemplo que cierre para siempre, explicando por qué.

prompt.es: Completa: «Al parecer, vendieron el local la semana pasada.»

feedback.es: Apparently introduce lo que parece cierto pero no está comprobado.

origin.text: ___, they sold the shop last week.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que descarta una alternativa con su prueba.

choices.text: We can rule out a thief, because it is possible.
We can rule out a thief, because nothing is missing.
We can rule out a thief, because the window is broken.

feedback.es: Rule out va acompañado de una prueba que lo justifique (nothing is missing); una ventana rota apoyaría al ladrón y «it is possible» no es una prueba.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la conclusión del hablante sobre el hombre.

choices.text: He is sure the man painted his own house.
He thinks the man took a ladder.
He thinks the man probably painted a wall, but he is not sure.

feedback.es: «It seems likely, although…» expresa una conclusión prudente: probable, pero no segura.

origin.audio: There is paint on his shoes, a ladder in his car and a new colour on the wall. Did he paint his house? It seems likely, although it could be a friend's house.

prompt.es: Elige la conclusión con el verbo más prudente.

choices.text: The lights and the car suggest that someone is home.
The lights and the car prove that someone is home.
The lights and the car are someone at home.

feedback.es: Con solo dos pistas, suggest es prudente; prove afirma más de lo que permiten las pruebas.

origin.text: Solo tienes dos pistas: las luces están encendidas y hay un coche fuera.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Esa alternativa es muy poco probable.»

feedback.es: Unlikely expresa que una alternativa casi se descarta sin cerrarla del todo.

prompt.es: Completa: «No podemos descartar esa posibilidad todavía.»

feedback.es: Rule out es la expresión para descartar; aquí va en infinitivo después de cannot.

origin.text: We cannot ___ out that possibility yet.
